what_it_is.prose: The BEL Integrated Counter Drone System (Atlas label 'V2') is the productionized form of DRDO's Integrated Drone Detection & Interdiction System (IDDIS), designed jointly by DRDO's CHESS (Centre for High Energy Systems and Sciences), LASTEC (Laser Science and Technology Centre) and LRDE laboratories and manufactured by Bharat Electronics Limited. The system combines a layered sensor stack — radar, RF direction-finder, and EO/IR — with two defeat layers: a soft-kill RF/GNSS jammer and a hard-kill fibre-laser Directed Energy Weapon. The IDDIS family has three operational marks: Mk-I (2 kW laser, ~1 km hard-kill range, first inducted March 2024 with the Indian Army), Mk-II (10 kW, 2 km range, cleared for induction by the Defence Acquisition Council on 29 December 2025), and Mk-IIA 'Sahastra Shakti' (30 kW, 5 km range, six 5 kW sources in a 2x3 configuration, effective against fixed-wing drones, swarms, and low-RCS missiles). A 300 kW 'Surya' variant targeting 20 km engagements is in development. The system's first reported combat intercept occurred on 13 April 2025 when a Mk-I unit operating with the XVI Corps shot down a Chinese-origin Pakistan-operated drone south of the Pir Panjal. IDDIS was subsequently deployed during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, where BEL confirmed it destroyed several low-RCS Pakistani drones. On 16 May 2025, BEL signed a ₹572 crore contract with the Indian Army's Corps of Army Air Defence for additional systems. The 'V2' label used in the Atlas corresponds most plausibly to the second-generation IDDIS architecture, which replaced the older DRDO D4 system; vendor confirmation of the exact version mapping is an open question.

stages.note: Soft kill RF/GNSS jammer (2-5 km) + hard kill fibre laser (0.8-5 km depending on variant)

deployments_procurement.summary: IDDIS Mk-I entered operational service with the Indian Army in March 2024 with the first lot of seven systems. The system achieved its first reported combat intercept on 13 April 2025 against a Pakistani-operated Chinese drone and was deployed operationally during Operation Sindoor in May 2025. The Defence Acquisition Council cleared Mk-II for induction on 29 December 2025, and BEL signed a ₹572 crore follow-on contract on 16 May 2025. Reports from November 2025 indicate a planned induction of 16 Mk-II systems across the Indian Army and IAF.

import_dependencies.summary: IDDIS is DRDO-designed and BEL-produced in India; the principal import dependency is the fibre-laser source for the directed-energy weapon. Early units (pre-2017 prototypes) imported the 1 kW-class fibre laser from Germany; the supply chain for production Mk-I/Mk-II/Mk-IIA units is not publicly itemised. FPGA and GaN RF amplifiers for the radar and jammer subsystems are industry-typically imported from the United States, but BEL has not confirmed vendor names.

faq.question: Is the BEL Integrated Counter Drone System the same as DRDO's D4 system?
faq.answer: They are related but distinct generations. D4 is the original DRDO counter-drone system (radar + EO + DF + RF/GPS jammer + LDEW). IDDIS (Integrated Drone Detection & Interdiction System) is the second-generation, laser-DEW-focused successor with three operational marks: Mk-I (2 kW), Mk-II (10 kW), and Mk-IIA 'Sahastra Shakti' (30 kW). The Atlas 'V2' label most plausibly corresponds to IDDIS.

faq.question: Has the system been used in combat?
faq.answer: Yes. On 13 April 2025, an IDDIS Mk-I unit operating with the Indian Army's XVI Corps conducted the first reported combat intercept of a Pakistani-operated Chinese-origin drone. The system was subsequently deployed during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, where BEL confirmed it destroyed several low-RCS Pakistani drones.

faq.question: What is the Sahastra Shakti variant?
faq.answer: Sahastra Shakti is the operational name for the IDDIS Mk-IIA variant, a 30 kW laser-DEW system using six 5 kW fibre-laser sources in a 2x3 configuration. It has an effective hard-kill range of approximately 5 km and is designed to engage fixed-wing drones, swarm drones, and low-RCS missiles.
